label: paragraph_title
text: YANGTSE COMPLEX.

label: paragraph_title
text: INSPECTING BRITISH GOODS SOCIETY:

label: text
text: SCHEME FOR BOYCOTT.

label: text
text: A fortnight ago the promoters of an anti-British boycott were getting busier.

label: text
text: They have organised an anti-British preaching society and these were lecturing any who would listen to them as to the heinous crimes of the British.

label: text
text: Then an inspection society for the examining of British goods and enforcing a boycott has also been formed.

label: text
text: According to the published programme of the latter they are first to tabulate the number of British merchant ships flying on the Yangtse, the number of banks established by the British in China, the number of factories, the different type of British banknotes, the number of British companies, concessions and pieces of land leased, the raw material and Chinese manufactured goods which are imported and exported by the British and the Chinese in the employ of the British. When all this information is gained they intend to take steps for a complete shut down of all British tons living in China, says the "Central China Post."

label: paragraph_title
text: Wanhsen Victims.

label: text
text: The Cabinet this morning decided to give grants to the families of the Chinese who lost their lives at Wanhai.

label: text
text: An appropriate mandate there-on will be issued shortly.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Hankow has also started a fund for the dependants of the British Naval men killed at Wanhsiem. The Shanghai fund has reached a respectable total. Hong Kong contributions should be sent to Mr. A. J. Bird, Chartered Bank (for disposal by the Navy League).

label: text
text: According to "Le Journal," the French Government has sent to Peking a diplomatic protest against shooting (on the Yangtse River) at the gunboat "Alerte."—Havas.

label: text
text: Paris, Oct. 21.

label: text
text: “Le Journal” states that the French Government has formally protested to Peking against the action of Southern troops on October 13, in firing on the French gunboat “Alerte,” killing one marine and seriously wounding another.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: OBREGON TO BE REAPPOINTED PRESIDENT.

label: text
text: Mexico City, Oct. 21.

label: text
text: The Chamber of Deputies has approved of an amendment to the Constitution enabling Obregon to be re-appointed. President of Mexico after an intervening presidency by somebody else. The Senate is likely to approve of the reform, which a majority of the States' legislatures must ratify.—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text:
Chicago, October 21.
The death is announced of the Socialist leader, Mr. Eugene Dohn five times a Presidential candidate, the last time when serving 10 years imprisonment on a charge of “advising disloyalty.” — Reuter's American Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: Peking, Oct. 21.

label: text
text: The Cabinet has decided to promulgate a mandate denouncing the opium evil.—Reuter.

label: text
text: A dog belonging to Revenue Officer Lanigan, of Cox's Path, Kowloon, showed symptoms of rabies and the animal was shot yesterday. The carcase has been sent to the Bacteriologist for examination.

label: paragraph_title
text: ASSAULT CASE.

label: text
text: STABBED A WAITER.

label: text
text: When three Chinese were charged before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning, with assaulting a restaurant "waiter," Mr. A. J. O. Donoghue was not present to defend the first two men. The case was about to be adjourned until to-morrow when Divisional Inspector Grant asked for permission to withdraw the charge against the two, as he had no evidence against them. These men were discharged and the case against the third man was continued.

label: text
text: The complainant said that the defendant made a threat on October 8, to do him harm for meddling with his affairs. At 2 o'clock the following morning, while he was seated outside a house at West Point, defendant with several others rushed at him and stabbed him on the left arm with a dagger. They then made their escape.

label: text
text: A district watchman "in evidence said that he heard cries "of "save life" and saw the complainant bleedingly profusely from the stab wound. He searched the vicinity and found the defendant disabled in the back yard of a house. The man had been injured by falling on an iron spike in trying to evade arrest.

label: text
text: Defendant, who denied that he was the assailant, was sentenced to six weeks' hard labour.

label: paragraph_title
text: SANK WITH SHIP.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINESE STEAMERS COLLIDE AT SAMSUI

label: text
text: 20 PASSENGERS DROWNED.

label: text
text: Some 20/steerage passengers are reported to have been drowned as a result of a collision between two Chinese river steamers of the smaller type on the Canton—Wuchow run.

label: text
text: The collision occurred about ten o'clock at night on Tuesday about forty minutes run out of Samsung, the West River.

label: text
text: One of the vessels (the "Leung Kwong") was badly holed near the bows and sank in a few minutes. The upper deck passengers were saved but, the whole of the steerage passengers are reported to have gone down with the vessel.

label: text
text: The "Tin Sing," the other vessel, was badly damaged but was able to keep afloat.

label: text
text: Both vessels, which run under the Chinese flag, were callers at Hong Kong in pre-strike times; the "Leung Kwong" being once on the Hong Kong—Canton run.

label: paragraph_title
text: CAFE THEFT.

label: paragraph_title
text: ABSCONDING EMPLOYEE CAUGHT.

label: text
text: RECOGNISED BY POLICE

label: text
text: A Chinese boy who absconded from the Cafe Albert in May last with a sum of money was recognised by a European police officer and arrested at Kowloon yesterday. This morning the boy was charged before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy with larceny by bailee of $290 and a bank paying-in book.

label: text
text: M. Albert Guetat, the proprietor of the Cafe, said that he sent the defendant to the bank to pay in two cheques and $20 in cash (total $290) which had been entered in the book, but he disappeared without carrying out his errand. Witness visited Kowloon yesterday and identified the defendant when he was pointed out by the police.

label: text
text: Defendant, said he lost the docubank and was afraid to return. He offered to repay the money in installments if complainant would take him back.

label: text
text: The Magistrate sentenced him to two months' hard labour.

label: paragraph_title
text: MALAY MAIL ON GESTURE MAKING.

label: paragraph_title
text: MORE MYSTERY.

label: text
text: Kuala Lumpur, October 13.— To-day, says Monday's "Malay Mail," makes another occasion in our political calendar that appears to have been specially marked for "gosture"-making purposes, this time by the F.M.S. and the Colony in collaboration. With only a day or two's notice given to the public, and with no word whatsoever by way of the preliminary explanation or justification, it has been arranged that H. E. the Governor will move in the Legislative Council, for approval of a loan

label: text
text: We know of course that Mr. Duff had to have his money, that the Crown Agents' endeavours to keep him out of the same had brought about damage to Malayan prestige which demanded early remedy, and that the financial juggling which the two legislative bodies of British Malaya to-day meet to approve may for all we are aware represent the best and more practical means of establishing that remedy. But we demand, as usual, to know why all this hush-hush business should be imperative. It appears to us illogical for Unofficials to exhibit themselves in penitent attitudes for their failure to detect and pounce upon departmental scandals, major and minor, which crop up so frequently, but never appear to be properly threshed out and responsibility therefore allocated, "while political decisions of really grave and far-reaching importance are watched and concluded in absolute secrecy, themselves consenting to be whistled up to "approve" these at impromptu Council meetings where at the public voice on essentially controversial matters never gets a chance of being heard. The above is merely by way of a general protest against what strikes us as a mischievous, cynical, and clearly growing tendency on the part of our existing administration to treat public opinion in this country as if it did not exist and Unofficial members as if they were a claque whose only province was to applaud the posturing protagonists of a political pantomime.

label: paragraph_title
text:
THE POPE ON FASCIST
TYRANNY.

label: text
text: The “Frankfurter Zeitung” reports that after the Pope’s recent refusal to allow the projected international Catholic gymnastic contest at the Vatican M. Thibaudeau, secretary of the French Catholic Young Men’s Associations, went to Rome in the hope of securing a withdrawal of the veto. In a personal audience the Pope plainly stated his reasons, and M. Thibaudeau has given them to the “Echo de Paris” as follows:—The Holy Father told us that he wished to take the opportunity to get past the Italian censorship and inform the whole world of the truth. The Italian press is unable to say anything; its freedom has been taken away, and the ill-informed foreign public knows nothing of what is going on in italy, where the Fascist Militiamen exercise their tyrannical power. The Government which owes everything to them and only exists thanks to their activity as powerless against them. And their leaders are tyrants to whom it is ureless to offer opposition.

label: paragraph_title
text: TRAFALGAR DAY.

label: text
text: CONCERT AND ZEEBRUGGE

label: text
text: NAVY LEAGUE DOINGS.

label: text
text: The annual celebration of Trafalgar Day was brought to a close yesterday evening when, under the auspices of the local branch of the Navy League, a grand concert, "under the distinguished patronage of H.E. the Governor (Sir Cecil Clementi, K.C.M.G.) and Lady Clementi, was held at the Queen's Theatre (by kind permission of Hong Kong Amusements, Ltd.) The audience was a large and distinguished one, among those present being noticed Sir Henry E. Pollock, K.C., Major-General C.C. Luard C.B., C.M.G., Rear-Admiral A. J. B. Stirling, C.B., R.N. and members of the Committee of the Navy League (Hong Kong branch).

label: text
text: The programme opened with an overture, "Plymouth 'Hod," admirably rendered by the Band of the 1st Batt. East Surrey Regt. (by kind permission of Bt. Col. F. S. Montague-Bates, C.B., C.M.G., D.S.O., and the officers of the 1st Batt. East Surreys).

label: paragraph_title
text: Trafalgnr's Memory.

label: text
text: Mr. R. A. Green followed with Anderson's "Drake goes West" which "showed his rich voice to advantage. Mrs. A. M. Bowes Smith always popular with Hong Kong audiences, received quite an ovation for her rendering of del Riego's "Homing," and responded with "By the Waters of Minnitonka" (Lawrence)—a delightful soupcon this.

label: text
text: Mr. L. E. Hopkins gave a stirring rendering of Leslie Stuart's Mighty Mother England," which rought the first part of the programme to a close.

label: text
text: During the interval a number of lantern slides depicting Nelson's famous flagship, the "Victory," the Battle of Trafalgar, and the Death of Nelson were thrown upon the screen, the theatre resounding with the cheering of the enthusiastic audience. It is difficult to understand why a Spanish waltz—the work of a German composer—was selected as appropriate for this item, but the audience disregarded the anomaly.

label: paragraph_title
text: Every Briton Should See.

label: text
text: "The second half of the programme comprised the much-advertised "Zeebrugge" film. As a stirring spectacle, it must be said at once that this is a picture possibly unsurpassed. Revealing, as it does, the elaborate preparations that were made by the British Admiralty prior to the famous raid on the mole, it certainly has a great educational value. Whether its screening at a time when Foreign Ministers of former rival Powers are "busying themselves with "Loving Cups" and fraternal greetings is judicious, it is not for the present critic to say. If parts of the film are perhaps, overdone, it is, generally speaking, most realistic—a film that could not fail to please an audience such as that which filled the Queen's Theatre last night. One is inclined to say that it is a film that every Briton should make a point of seeing."

label: paragraph_title
text: Facts About the Naval Epic of 1918.

label: text
text: It was on April 22, 1918 that the British Navy earned immortal memory by a feat, daring but skilfully planned.

label: text
text: The main purpose of the enterprise was to block the harbours of Zéebrugge and Ostend.

label: text
text: Three old cruisers "Iphigenia," "Thetis" and "Intrepid" filled with cement were to enter the harbour and be sunk at the entrance to the ship canal to Bruges. The "Vindictive" (not the ship now on this station), supported by two auxiliary vessels, was to assault the mole on its outer and Western

label: text
text: side, and by creating an impression that this was the main operation, divert the enemies fire from the blocking ships. The chief obstacle to the enterprise lay in the powerful batteries which were camouflaged behind the Dunes.

label: text
text: The "Vindiclive" (Capt. Alfred B. Carpenter) aided by "Iris" (Comm. Valentine Gibbs) and "Daffodil" (Lt. Harold Campbell) were detailed off to attack the outer side of the mole. Two submarines C1 and C3 under Lt. Aubrey Newbold and Lt. Richard D. Sandford respective

Fifteen destroyers stood by to screen the Zeebrugge monitors. Eighteen large coastal motor boats under the command of Lt. Arthur E. Weiman accompanied the expedition. label: paragraph_title
text: Nine V.C's.

label: text
text: There were 50 officers and 980 men of the Royal Navy and 35 officers and 718 men of the Royal Marines engaged in this attack. The casualties at the end of this engagement, which lasted barely an hour, amounted to 687 killed, wounded and missing. There were 9 V.C's awarded and innumerable other decorations for gallantry.

label: text
text: The blocking of Zeebraugge offered a good prospect of success and was within reasonable distance of it. If it did not wholly succeed the work of those who took part in its sent a breath of inspiration through the Navy and gave all who took part in it, a lasting name. At any rate, this nest of enemy submarines was seriously tested.

label: paragraph_title
text: INTERNATIONAL KINEMA CONGRESS.

label: text
text: Paris, September 30.—The International Cinematograph Congress at Paris dealt with many interesting questions and passed a resolution in favour of historical accuracy in the presentation of historical films, and also recommending film producers to avoid staging films likely to arouse international bad feeling.

label: text
text: It was maintained that the villain of the piece ought to be of the same nationality as the author or producer.

label: text
text: The Congress recognised the necessity of an International Cinema matograph Institution to deal with the exchange of films to be attached to the League of Nations, and resolved to found as soon as possible an International Federation of the Cinematographic Press.
